claim.quote: While the analysis of these datasets has not yielded statistically significant results, the developed methods provide a solid basis for future measurements with the KM3NeT detector.

date.note: Date recorded is the arXiv preprint submission date; no journal publication record was found/fetched this session, so date_kind is 'preprint'.

key_value_text.quote: The study uses the dataset collected with the first KM3NeT/ARCA configurations with 6, 8, 19, and 21 active detection units, corresponding to a total livetime of 640 days.
key_value_text.value: All-sky single-flavour astrophysical flux (single power law, 68% credible level): phi0 = 3.0(+2.1/-2.0)x10^-18 GeV^-1 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1, spectral index gamma = 3.00(+0.30/-0.35). No constraint obtained for the Galactic Ridge fit at current sensitivity. Based on the first KM3NeT/ARCA configurations (6, 8, 19, 21 active detection units), 640 days total livetime.

name: Search for an all-sky and a Galactic Ridge diffuse neutrino emission with the first 2 years of KM3NeT/ARCA data
notes: Added as an optional (non-mandatory) third result to give KM3NeT full flagship depth (2-4 results required; 3 provided). result_type 'limit' because the abstract reports upper limits and explicitly states no statistically significant excess was found.

significance.locator: Abstract, arXiv:2608.06163 (no significant excess found; upper limits reported instead of significance)
significance.note: No statistically significant excess was found; the abstract reports upper limits on the diffuse astrophysical flux rather than a significance.

summary.plain: KM3NeT/ARCA searched two years of early data for a steady glow of cosmic neutrinos from the whole sky and from the Milky Way's central band, and found no significant signal, only limits.
summary.technical: Diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux search using KM3NeT/ARCA's first configurations (6, 8, 19, 21 active detection units; 640 days livetime): all-sky single-power-law fit phi0 = 3.0(+2.1/-2.0)x10^-18 GeV^-1 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1, gamma = 3.00(+0.30/-0.35) at 68% credible level; no significant excess, upper limits derived for both the all-sky and Galactic Ridge searches.

title: Search for an all-sky and a Galactic Ridge diffuse neutrino emission with the first 2 years of KM3NeT/ARCA data
why_it_matters: Diffuse-flux and Galactic Ridge searches probe the population of astrophysical neutrino sources as a whole and test consistency with IceCube's diffuse flux measurements from the Southern Hemisphere.
